kicker: Hugging Face and GitHub are the AI village's two shared wells — anyone can draw from them, but you need to know which water is clean.
summary: Get models from Hugging Face and code from GitHub — check the source, the license and the file format before you download.

quiz.q: You find two copies of the same model: one from the original author, a .gguf file with a clear license; one re-uploaded by a stranger, a .pkl file with more downloads. Which do you pick?
options: The stranger's, since it's already compressed
Download both, see which runs faster
quiz.explain: Downloads don't prove safety. A .pkl file can run code the moment it is opened; the original with a clear license is the safer choice.

wells.label: Two wells
wells.art: A moonlit night at the edge of the village: two mossy stone wells side by side on a flagstone yard, under one bamboo pulley beam with a lantern hanging at each end. The left well is GitHub, lines of code glinting in its water; the right is Hugging Face, holding small labelled clay jars — models and data. A bamboo bucket hangs in front between them, a paper tag on it saying what you need.
wells.prompt: Drag the bucket to the well that has what you need
wells.aria: Two wells: GitHub and Hugging Face. Drop the bucket into the well that has what you need

depth.label: A deepening well
depth.art: A moonlit night and an old well cut in half from mouth to floor: the moon hangs over the mouth, a cone of moonlight full of dust falls down the shaft, the courses of stone curve round its wall and darken with depth; outside the cut lie layers of earth, pine roots and a vein of wet gravel seeping into the well. A pine and a stone lantern stand on the bank. The water column is the number of public models: drag the moon's reflection up the water, it rises past three dates carved by a groove, clay jars of models bob up thicker and thicker until, today, they cover the surface.
depth.prompt: Drag the moon's reflection up the water
depth.next: Keep dragging up — the water rises to today's mark
depth.aria: A deepening well: public models on Hugging Face over the years. Drag the moon's reflection up the water, or use the up and down arrow keys

fact.text: In September 2024, Hugging Face co-founder Clément Delangue announced the hub had passed 1 million public models.

milestones.label: The engine for local AI moves in

fact.text: 20 Feb 2026: the team behind the engine that runs AI on personal computers (llama.cpp, you'll meet it in the next station) joined Hugging Face; both say the project stays open.
On 15 Oct 2026 Hugging Face's Models page counted over 3 million public models.

insight.text: Over 3 million models — nobody can look at them all; what to learn is how to filter.

detail.text: On 15 Oct 2026 Hugging Face's Models page counted 3,156,130 public models; the number changes every day.

card.label: Reading the well stone
card.art: On the mossy ground at the edge of the village stands a low stele, seen three-quarters under the moon, a stone lantern to its right. A damp sheet of washi is tied over its face, hiding six carved lines. Take the ink pad from the inkstone and dab the paper from the top down: ink takes only where the stone stands up, so each carved line comes out white on black. In front of the stele a puddle reflects it.
card.prompt: Take the ink pad and dab the paper to read each carved line
card.task: Your job: writing sales captions, on a 16 GB laptop
card.order: One line at a time, from the top — dab line {n} first
card.aria: A mock model card: six lines to read before you download a model
card.mock: A made-up model for learning, not a real one

lines.label: Name & author
lines.read: Who is the author, and do they have an official page? Is this the original, or someone else's copy or compressed version?

lines.label: Parameters
lines.read: 8B: 8 billion parameters — the number tells you how big the model is; the bigger, the heavier for your machine.

lines.label: License
lines.read: It decides whether you may use it commercially, change it or share it. “other” means you have to open the separate terms and read them.
lines.verdict: Open the terms before using it for clients

lines.label: File format
lines.read: GGUF, 4-bit compressed: a compact kind of file that runs on a laptop.

lines.label: Downloads
lines.read: It shows the model is popular — not that it is safe or good.
lines.verdict: Popular is not proof of safe

lines.label: Limits & warnings
lines.value: Not well tested in Vietnamese; may get figures wrong
lines.read: A careful author says plainly where the model is weak. A stone that says nothing about limits is a sign to be wary.
lines.verdict: Vietnamese captions: test it yourself first

insight.text: Read these 6 lines and you know: who made it, whether it fits your machine, and what you may use it for.

detail.text: A license of “other” means the author wrote their own terms; open the link and read them before using it for clients.

card.decode: This stone is a model card — the introduction page that comes with a model on Hugging Face.

repo.label: Two houses
repo.art: A raked gravel island in black water under the moon, with two wooden houses whose curved roofs look identical from the front — each house is a repo (a code store) on GitHub. Round each house are things that tell its story: the introduction scroll, the roof lamp, the worn path, the mailbox, the notice board, the gate sign. Walk round the back to compare them, then light the gate lamp of the house you trust.
repo.prompt: Walk round behind the two houses, then light the real one's lamp
repo.aria: Compare two GitHub repos on six signals, then choose the one to trust
repo.hint: Drag to walk round the island, or use the arrow keys when the view is focused; wheel or pinch to move closer. Tap a thing to read that signal on both houses; light a gate lamp to choose a house.
repo.signalAria: Signal {label}: see it on both houses

signals.label: README
signals.what: The front page: what it does, how to install it, examples.

signals.label: Stars
signals.what: How many people bookmarked it: popularity, not a guarantee of safety.

signals.label: Forks
signals.what: Copies others made to change on their own. A fake repo is often a renamed copy.

signals.label: Issues
signals.what: Where people report bugs and ask questions. Recent replies mean someone still looks after it.

signals.label: Releases
signals.what: Published versions with notes. Downloading from here is safer than grabbing stray files.

signals.label: License
signals.what: With no license, by default you may not copy, change or distribute it.

values.license: MIT – an open license: you may use, change and resell it, just credit the author

values.readme: Copied from the original, plus a “quick installer” button

repo.mock: Two made-up repos for learning — each house is a repo (a code store) on GitHub
repo.pickAria: Choose repo {name} as the one to trust
repo.right: Right. The original has a history, someone looking after it, and a clear license.
repo.wrong: Look closely at the name: “rn” is pretending to be “m”. The stars are almost equal, but the history and the care are completely different.

insight.text: Crooks copy famous repos, add malware and re-upload them under near-identical names — the star count won't tell you apart.

detail.text: A repo without a license falls under default copyright: the author keeps all rights and you may not copy it freely.

clean.label: Filtering the water
clean.art: Seen low beside a big dark bowl: a bamboo spout at the back pours murky water down three stone basins that come toward you. Each basin holds one kind of dirt: a code scroll stamped “lang-rnau” in red, a fizzing “.pkl” jar, a license crossed out “no commercial use”. On the left bank lie three woven bamboo filters: Right author, Right format, Right license. Set the right filter in a basin and its water clears; with all three in, the bowl fills with clear water holding the whole moon.
clean.prompt: Drag each filter to the basin holding what it stops
clean.aria: Three filters before you download a model or some code. Drag each filter to the basin holding what it stops; or pick a filter, then a basin, or press 1, 2, 3 on a filter
clean.filterAria: Filter “{label}”: drag it to a basin, or press 1, 2, 3 to set it in that basin

debris.label: A .pkl file: opening it can run code

clean.pickFirst: Drag a filter to this basin — or pick a filter first
clean.picked: Now touch the basin holding what “{label}” stops
left: One murky basin left — drag the last filter
Two murky basins left — drag the next filter

insight.text: Three filters before you download: the right author, the right license, a .safetensors or .gguf file instead of .pkl.

detail.text: In 2024 the security firm JFrog found models on Hugging Face with malware built in, running by itself when the pickle file was opened.

clean.note: GGUF and safetensors hold only data, so they are safer than pickle — but no format is perfectly safe: the right source still matters.

t31-hf-ggml.title: GGML and llama.cpp join HF to ensure the long-term progress of Local AI

t31-repo-confusion.title: Millions of Malicious Repositories Flood GitHub
t31-repo-confusion.note: Reports research on “repo confusion” by the security firm Apiiro: popular repos cloned, infected with malware and re-uploaded under the same name. Exact numbers are hard to count because repos are constantly deleted and re-uploaded.

t31-hf-pickle.title: Pickle Scanning
t31-hf-pickle.note: Explains why loading a pickle file can run arbitrary code; the Hub's scanner is “not 100% foolproof”.

t31-jfrog.title: Data Scientists Targeted by Malicious Hugging Face ML Models with Silent Backdoor
t31-jfrog.note: JFrog reported about 100 flagged models; according to Ars Technica, JFrog said about 10 were truly malicious and most of the rest were research experiments.
